As Americans prepare for the nation’s 250th anniversary, a new study reveals Ohio has the highest risk of backyard fireworks accidents, property damage and related injuries in the country.

The analysis, conducted by sports betting site The Action Network and reported by ABC 6, examined fireworks trade shipment data, real-time consumer search behavior and state laws across the country to rank the risk of amateur pyrotechnics by state.

According to the findings, an active fireworks participant in Ohio faces a 3.54 percent chance of a holiday mishap or property flare-up, which translates to a 1-in-28 chance. Researchers attributed the high risk to the state’s massive shipment volume — amounting to $3.50 per person — and a high consumer interest score.

“Because full aerial cakes and reloadable mortar shells are legal, large multi-family block parties in the Buckeye State carry the highest statistical chance of a backyard mishap or property flare-up in the nation,” the study states.

The Midwest registered the highest concentration of high-risk states, with Indiana, Missouri and Kansas joining Ohio in the top five.

New study reveals Ohio has the highest risk of backyard fireworks accidents, property damage and related injuries in the country ( Getty Images/iStockphoto )

Indiana ranked second with a 1-in-34 chance of an accident. The state imports $3.89 per capita in fireworks and serves as a primary “border-hopping” pipeline for residents traveling from neighboring Illinois, where aerial fireworks are legally banned.

Missouri ranked third with a 1-in-36 chance. The study found that Missouri functions as the corporate distribution capital of the fireworks industry, clearing $85.7 million in direct imports, or $13.84 per person.

New Hampshire and Kansas rounded out the top five highest-risk states, with a 1-in-39 and 1-in-40 chance of accidents, respectively.

By contrast, Massachusetts was identified as the state with the lowest overall fireworks risk, carrying a 0.02 percent — or 1-in-5,000 — chance of a mishap. The study credited this low rate to the state’s strict and actively enforced consumer fireworks bans.

Though federal data indicates between 13,004 and 14,700 emergency room visits across the United States each year, the study shows that epidemiologists estimate the actual number of minor, home-treated burns and localized property fires is four to 10 times higher than official hospital records show.

According to the report, Americans consume 322.4 million pounds of fireworks every year.

News.title: Katie Boulter breaks down in tears over marriage question after Wimbledon exit
News.content:
Katie Boulter was in tears following her surprise defeat in the first round here on Tuesday and her misery summed up the desperate experience of the British big names at this Wimbledon.

There was an expectation on Court 3 that, after the home contingent lost all 10 of their encounters on Monday, Boulter would break the drought having already reached the third round twice before and pour just a little solace on the bonfire of the Brits.

But in the event, the world No 60’s challenge quickly went up in flames as she was comfortably dispatched 6-4, 6-2 by an 18-year-old qualifier ranked outside the top 150. With Jack Draper and Emma Raducanu withdrawing in the build-up and Cameron Norrie losing to his own qualifier in American Michael Zheng, this completed the ignominy for the quartet.

In fact, this could have been the worst of the lot. There can be no doubt that in Tyra Caterina Grant, the daughter of a former NBA player, Italy has a star for the future, but nobody anticipated the manner of this shock. This was Grant’s debut in a grand slam and only her fourth appearance on grass after coming through three games at Roehampton last week to take her place in the main draw.

However, she blew away Boulter with her powerful serving, emphatic groundstrokes and a game blessed with variety. Boulter, who just two weeks ago beat world No 2 Elena Rybakina on her way to the semi-finals at Queen’s, had no answer and was still coming to terms with her exit when she fronted the media a few hours later. It was a query referencing her impending nuptials to Australian player Alex de Minaur that prompted the outpouring of emotions.

“I think this is the most challenging part about tennis. It’s so difficult to feel satisfied. I think it’s something you keep trying to strive for, but yeah…” she replied after being asked if this was still going to be the best month of her life. “Yeah, it’s tough. It’s tough. I can assure you it’s going to be the best day of my life in a while. But not today.”

The irony was that De Minaur was next on Court 3 after Boulter’s elimination and the world No 6 coped admirably in seeing off Argentinian Roman Andres Burruchaga 7-6, 6-1, 6-0 despite his fiancée’s distress.

News.title: Suspected Marburg outbreak in Uganda prompts US alert
News.content:
The US embassy in Uganda has issued an alert over reports of a potential Marburg case in the country’s western region.

“The US Embassy is aware there are reports of a potential case of Marburg Virus Disease, a viral haemorrhagic fever, in western Uganda,” it said in the advisory, which was published on Monday.

As of Tuesday, Uganda’s health ministry had yet to release any information on the suspected outbreak, which remains unconfirmed.

Uganda has extensive experience with dealing with outbreaks of haemorrhagic fevers and last reported a Marburg outbreak in 2017, when there were four cases and three deaths.

The country has previously sought to downplay the impact of haemorrhagic fever outbreaks in effort to protect its burgeoning tourism industry.

A message on the health ministry’s homepage, just beneath a link to its dashboard tracking the spread of Ebola, reads: “Ministry of Health is in control. No need for panic. Uganda is safe!”

However it is currently battling to control an outbreak of Ebola imported from neighbouring Congo, which could complicate any outbreak response effort.

So far, Uganda has reported a total of 20 cases of the rare Bundibugyo species of Ebola, with 15 of them imported from the DRC.

The World Health Organization (WHO) is aware of the reports of a potential Marburg case, The Telegraph understands.

News.title: This is not a drill: Germany lose a World Cup penalty shoot-out
News.content:
“I do not have much to say. This is now my second World Cup and we have missed moving onto the next round twice now in a row. I want to apologise for that. We are all very disappointed. We had many plans for this year’s World Cup. It is not a very good feeling to disappoint again. The team tried a lot. One goal was disallowed. We had a very strong opponent; it was difficult to create chances and keep the pace. The Paraguayan team defended very deep and it was difficult to run for a long time. We tried to move over the flanks but unfortunately, it did not really work out. I do not think we deserved to win this time.

“I do not think we allowed many chances. We were on the ball, in the momentum, especially after the equaliser. We ended up in the shoot-out. It was not easy because I missed that penalty kick and it is a 50/50 chance. During the tournament, you really have to give it your all. I do not think we played bad football, but something was always missing and that was the case today as well. As players, we need to look at ourselves and what we can do better. We play for such a big football nation. If you get eliminated early, you do not deserve to stay.”

News.title: Djokovic revels in role of pantomime villain... and earns wedding invite
News.content:
Has anyone in sport ever revelled with quite such gusto as Novak Djokovic at feeling like the world is against them? At one set all here, the Wimbledon crowd had, in the words of John McEnroe, turned very vocally from thinking “who?” to chants of “Wuuuu” in support of the Chinese underdog Wu Yibing.

The world No 99 had not just quietly got himself back into the match after losing the first set, but was actually beginning to dictate with his rasping forehand as the players traded games to 4-4 in the third.

Djokovic took exception previously to the Wimbledon crowd supporting Holger Rune against him and, with just about every losing point here prompting an ever louder cry of “Wuuuu”, the 39-year-old seven-time champion looked suddenly both irritated and energised.

A sensational passing shot interspersed with some brilliantly dogged hitting from the back of the court clinched a crucial third-set service break, with Djokovic then celebrating not with a clenched fist but by pointedly holding a prolonged finger to his ear.

Djokovic’s son, Stefan, was also off his feet with a huge fist pump before his father fought off a series of break points to hold serve and move two sets to one ahead with a defiant arm to the sky.

News.title: Gabriel Martinelli the unlikely saviour after Japan make Brazil look average
News.content:
Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of Brazil vs Japan in the 2026 World Cup round of 32.

The two sides meet at Houston Stadium with temperatures are expected to be in the mid-thirties, which should favour Carlo Ancelotti’s men over their Japanese opponents, but there is plenty of intrigue for the match ahead this evening.

Brazil have no suspensions to worry about, but there are two key questions for fitness. Raphinha is expected to miss the match with a hamstring problem, and he could be a longer-term absence if they manage to get through to the next round.

Another question hangs over Santos, with the 34-year-old still yet to prove his full fitness, while Rayan, Matheus Cunha and Vinicius Jr. have done little wrong so far. A draw against Morocco was followed by wins against Haiti and Scotland to give them top spot in Group C, but it’s fair to say they have not truly been tested so far.

Japan have their own injury over Takefusa Kubo, who has a knee problem from the 2-2 draw with the Netherlands. The side drew 1-1 with Sweden, but managed to defeat Tunisia 4-0. Like Brazil, they are yet to really dominate a quality side, so they also have something to prove.

Right now, France lead Argentina as favourites to win the tournament, but Brazil are alongside Spain, England and Germany as the next sides most likely to secure glory. A confident win over Japan might start to change minds and build momentum.

Japan should not be overawed, though. They defeated Brazil 3-2 last year in October in Tokyo, coming from behind for a famous win.

The winner here will face the victor of tomorrow’s match between Ivory Coast and Norway.

News.title: Norrie’s silver lining to first-round exit... he can now attend own stag do
News.content:
Given his pedigree as a fierce grass-court competitor, few would have predicted Cameron Norrie to fall in the opening round at Wimbledon for the first time in eight years.

But as the only seeded British player at this year’s Championships walked off court after his arm-wrestle of a match against American Michael Zheng, a qualifier ranked 115 places below him, even he might be able to see one small silver lining. Norrie will at least be free to attend his own stag do in Ibiza the weekend after next.

Norrie was a quarter-finalist here last year and reached the semi-finals in 2022, so a deep run at this year’s tournament might have resulted in a scheduling mishap. But he can breathe easy after suffering a 6-7, 6-2, 6-7, 6-3, 7-6 defeat by the world No 144, which will at least free him up for the big bash on Wimbledon finals weekend.

“It always stinks to lose, especially at Wimbledon, my favourite tournament in the world, a tournament I always play so well at,” said Norrie, who will marry his American fiancée Louise Jacobi in December. “There’s no hiding from it. Yeah, it stinks. Especially tomorrow, everyone is still in the tournament, and you’re out. You’re just wanting to play. So it’s tough.”

News.title: UAE-backed Sudan rebels ‘training in Libya’
News.content:
Sudanese rebel fighters are being trained to use drones, heavy machine guns and rocket launchers in a network of secret camps in Libya, investigators have claimed.

Lighthouse Reports, a Dutch non-profit media organisation, alleged that southern Libya has become a key hub for training and supplying the Rapid Support Forces (RSF), the paramilitary group that has been repeatedly accused of war crimes and genocide in Sudan’s civil war.

Drawing on interviews with RSF defectors and Libyan National Army (LNA) officers, and open source analysis, the investigators detail how Sudanese fighters receive training from UAE-backed Colombian mercenaries and Libyan soldiers.

The video investigation, which was produced in conjunction with Sudan War Monitor, a group of journalists and open-source researchers, and Evident Media, a non-profit visual investigation organisation, is the latest contribution to a growing body of evidence that the conflict in Sudan has evolved into a regional proxy war.

Earlier this year, Reuters reported that thousands of RSF fighters had undergone training in a secret camp in Ethiopia. The UAE has long been widely accused of backing the RSF – allegations it has repeatedly denied.

Sports.title: Tottenham WIN staggering £85million Mateus Fernandes transfer race with Man Utd not willing to pay huge price tag

Sports.title: Jurgen Klopp refuses to rule out return to management during World Cup TV appearance
Sports.content:
JURGEN KLOPP refused to rule out replacing Julian Nagelsmann as Germany coach after Die Mannschaft were sent packing from the World Cup on penalties.

Former Liverpool boss Klopp was immediately made the front-runner to take over following the shoot-out defeat to Paraguay, even though Nagelsmann insisted he would NOT quit.





Klopp, now head of global football for the Red Bull group, has been one of Nagelsmann’s most persistent critics in the USA.

He has hinted that he would like to get back into management and pressed on his possible plans, Klopp, working as a TV pundit on the game, said: “I understand that my name is being mentioned.

“But this isn’t the moment to talk about it – and certainly not with me.”

Klopp slammed Nagelsmann’s tactics but also made it clear that German football will have to be restructured on his terms if he is to be tempted to be the nation’s saviour.

He added: “There are 500,000 ways to win a football match. You just have to find one.

“There was only one goal, one dream, and that’s been shattered. It was dramatic. We didn’t function and didn’t create enough.

“We all know how well the lads can play, but they didn’t bring that to the pitch. In three months we’ll be raving about Florian Wirtz and Jamal Musiala again, about how great they are.

“But not now. We can talk about the DFB (German FA).



WORLD CUP 2026 FREE BETS AND SIGN UP OFFERS

“We absolutely have to change a few things. We can start with the U10s and wait a few years to see what happens at the top level.”

Nagelsmann, meanwhile, whose contract runs to 2028 after it was renewed last year, vowed: “I am not someone who runs away. That’s not who I am.

“I am not going to resign just because we’ve been eliminated

“I’m sure if you did a survey now and talked to all the people in Germany I don’t think they would speak very positively about me.

“Everybody knows how I work and everybody knows my style of football.



“This isn’t the time to talk about the nitty gritty; the guys know what kind of manager I am.

“If the DFB wants me to stay I will stay but I know how football works.

“I also know that a lot of people want me to leave but it is up to the DFB. If they think somebody else can do a better job than that is their decision.”

Nagelsmann, though, is likely to be sacked in the coming days after legend Lothar Matthaus revealed how his decision to allow the players’ families regular access to the camp caused major rows.

Matthaus said: “One player was angry with another because their mother was allowed to fly along, while some families went with the team and other wives and children had to go on commercial flights.

“There was a lot of unrest. But despite all that, the focus simply wasn’t on this World Cup. It was always a free family day and another free family day.

Sports.title: Tino Livramento undergoes surgery after being forced to leave England’s World Cup squad
Sports.content:
TINO LIVRAMENTO has successfully undergone surgery after picking up an injury on World Cup duty.

The Newcastle full-back was forced to withdraw from the England squad just days before their opener against Croatia.





According to the Magpies, Livramento has completed the minor surgical procedure for the sustained calf injury.

The star featured from the bench in England’s friendly against New Zealand but it was not meant to be as Chelsea‘s Trevoh Chabolah was announced as his replacement.

Newcastle wished him a speedy recovery and said that they expect him to return during pre-season.

It was a sorry sight to see as the 23-year-old exited early from the Fifa tournament.

The ex-Chelsea and Southampton youngster also missed the back end of the Premier League season as Newcastle trudged to a 12th-placed finish.

In May, Toon boss Eddie Howe quashed speculation surrounding Livramento’s inclusion in the squad and whether he would miss out due to his lurking injury.

Howe said: “Tino, we think, will be fine. If the season was to go on for another couple of weeks, he’d be back for us.

“It wasn’t a serious injury, and it looks like he is moving well on the grass now.”



WORLD CUP 2026 FREE BETS AND SIGN UP OFFERS

But once Livramento’s exit was confirmed, Thomas Tuchel said: “Tino was, of course, very disappointed and very sad.

“All of us were. It was kind of a little shock in training.

“When he stopped training, he straight away had the feeling that this can be an injury that cost him the tournament and he was unfortunately right.

“After assessment, we got the information that it’s an injury of about four or five weeks, which is unfortunately too long to keep on like rebuilding and reintegrating him into the squad, so we took the decision to send him home.”



Livramento’s future seems as if it is anything but certain as transfer rumours are rampant.

The Croydon-born ace has been linked with a move to Man City throughout 2026 even if Howe has cast doubt on the transfer.

Sports.title: Inside South London footie club where England’s Djed Spence and £50m DR Congo World Cup star played as kids
Sports.content:
SOUTH LONDON’S finest will face off against each other when England’s Djed Spence takes on Aaron Wan-Bissaka’s DR Congo in Atlanta on Wednesday.

But the real bragging rights belong to a youth club called Junior Elite from Beckenham in the south of the capital that can proudly boast the World Cup pair as two of their own.





Tottenham star Spence, who looks to be Thomas Tuchel’s last right-back standing, began playing for Junior Elite at Under-9 level in the same team as Emile Smith Rowe.

While West Ham man Wan-Bissaka, who switched allegiances from England to the Democratic Republic of Congo last year, started at the academy side even earlier aged six.

Colin Omogbehin is first-team coach at Fulham but has been running Junior Elite for decades and is thrilled to see the club’s former sons vying on football’s grandest stage.

The 51-year-old told SunSport: “It’s a real historic moment and something that not many grassroots clubs can say has happened to them so we’re really proud.”



Few people in football know both Spence and Wan-Bissaka better than Omogbehin, who has welcomed both back to the club throughout their professional careers.

The duo may well start at right-back for their respective nations on Wednesday.

But the fresh-faced Spence with a Mohican haircut that Omogbehin remembers was a right-winger, finishing off fine moves at the back post.

While Wan-Bissaka was a six-year-old centre-forward, playing up a year because there was no Under-7 team, capable of acrobatics few other kids could when he first started.



WORLD CUP 2026 FREE BETS AND SIGN UP OFFERS

Both have had to deal with setbacks in their professional careers, whether it be Wan-Bissaka struggling to justify his £50million price tag at Manchester United or Spence waiting two-and-a-half YEARS for his Spurs debut.

But their resilience is a strength that has propelled their careers to this landmark moment, according to Omogbehin, along with their adaptability and determination.

The Cottagers coach said: “Both players are very football intelligent, they’ve got real good game understanding

“But at the same time, it’s their character, their ability to be able to deal with adversity. And I saw that from a young age in both of these players.

“Djed was a fine athlete who technically got better and better. But I wouldn’t say Djed was the best in his group. And I think Djed would say that as well.



“He was in a group where about five or six players went on to academies quite early.

“And when you’re seeing all your team-mates moving and you’re not, you could lose a little bit of confidence.

“But he kept going and he’s ended up arguably having the best career out of all those guys. And nobody could have seen that coming.

CLICK ON PIC FOR STAR’S PROFILE

“He came to us at Fulham and it was hard for him. He worked so hard to get a scholarship. A lot of players got scholarships before him. He could be arguably seen as a late developer.



“He’s always fighting against the system. He’s had a lot of adversity early in his career.

“But he’s always had the resilience and the mindset to overcome it.”

Omogbehin says it was not always plain-sailing either for Wan-Bissaka, whom he describes as “quite a shy and introverted young man”.

The 28-year-old left Junior Elite for Crystal Palace where he switched from centre-forward to right-wing, but at one stage as a teenager he was on the verge of release.

That was until he was tried out as a full-back due to lack of alternatives in a training session and excelled from there.



As Omogbehin observed, Wan Bissaka “managed to find a way to fight and stay in”, just when it looked like his football journey could be over.

Omogbehin credits the influence of key family-members on both players’ success stories.

Wan-Bissaka’s dad Ambroise is “a wonderfully grounded, humble and structured” father who is “a man of his word”.

Spence’s ever-present mother Aisha has been an “unbelievable driving force” who used to take her son to Junior Elite practice early to do running drills before training.



Speed has been one of Spence’s biggest assets on the pitch ever since he was little, with Omogebehin remembering him as “like a Rolls Royce who just floated across the grass” when in a Junior Elite shirt.

While on Wan-Bissaka, Omogebehin recalled: “You haven’t really seen Aaron do it in his professional career, but it’s not many times you see an under-seven score from an overhead kick.

“The cross comes in, he’s back to goal, overhead kick, six years of age. That’s when we thought, ‘we might have somebody here’.”

Of course, Wan-Bissaka could be competing with Spence right now for a place in England’s defence had he not switched to DR Congo.

The Croydon lad played three times for England’s Under-21 side and was even called up to the seniors in 2019, but had to pull out through injury.



He came up during an era of fierce competition at right-back including Kyle Walker, Trent Alexander-Arnold, Kieran Trippier and Reece James.

Wan-Bissaka, who also faced the Three Lions when playing for the Congolese Under-17 side, eventually decided to change countries in 2025.

Omogbehin added: “I’ve never really had a discussion with him about that.



“But I know there was a period of time where he was playing exceptionally well and the call-up never came.

“I think DR Congo really, really wanted him. His family are Congolese.

“He’s Congolese and he’s made his decision. And I think it’s one that he’s really happy about.”

Omogbehin has presented both Wan-Bissaka and Spence with framed Junior Elite shirts when they have played against Fulham in recent years.

Wan-Bissaka has been back for presentations at his old academy club, spending hours signing autographs and taking pictures with the current crop of kids.



Omogbehin sees the same personalities in both that he did all those years ago, with Spence still “an original, cool, good guy” who has his “swagger” and Wan-Bissaka still that “nice young man” who is “very quiet”.

Junior Elite are currently on a summer break so had no plans to get together to watch their old players compete in the World Cup last 32 – until urged to by SunSport!

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Omogbehin added: “We might sit together with the old coaches back involved and watch.

“Because there’s a lot of people that are proud of these young men and have played a part in seeing their development.”

Sports.title: Hero World Cup fan tackles gunman at watch party before police officer saves his life after bullet severed artery
Sports.content:
A HEROIC World Cup fan tackled a gunman before being saved by a police officer.

The courageous fan’s life was saved after a bullet severed an artery at a watch party.





Luis Romero of Duarte, California, is recovering in hospital after a shooting at the watch party in the Koreatown area of Los Angeles.

He was watching the Group A game between Mexico and South Korea with his son on Thursday, June 18.

An armed individual then began opening fire towards the fans.

Romero managed to tackle the gunman.



However, the father collapsed after a round was fired into his leg and severed a major artery.

This caused Romero to bleed out before being saved by LAPD Officer Helen Zhang.

The LAPD Officer stopped Romero’s bleeding by applying a tourniquet to his leg.

It occurred on the same day that a shooting occurred in New York City’s Times Square that left one individual wounded.

Sports.title: World Cup LIVE: England face extreme weather nightmare as Donald Trump ally mocks Iran
Sports.content:
Paraguay's players celebrate celebrate after winning the penalty shootout during the 2026 World Cup round of 32 football match between Germany and Paraguay at the Boston Stadium in Foxborough on June 29, 2026. (Photo by FRANCK FIFE / AFP via Getty Images)

Canada, Brazil, Paraguay and Morocco are all through to the round of 16, while more mouth-watering World Cup ties await on Tuesday night

Germany and Netherlands have both been knocked out of the World Cup following shock round of 32 defeats to Paraguay and Morocco respectively.

Julian Nagelsmann's side went into the tie as strong favourites to progress to the last 16 after topping Group E and facing a Paraguay side who scraped through as the seventh best third place team in the tournament.

But football doesn't seem to work like that, as Paraguay stunned their opponents to win on penalties following a 1-1 draw after extra-time. Julio Enciso, the former Brighton midfielder, opened the scoring for Paraguay in the first half before Arsenal's Kai Havertz levelled after the break.

Although the South American missed two opportunities to win the shootout, they still kept their nerve to run out 4-3 winners on spot-kicks and secure a place in the Round of 16 against either France or Sweden.

Netherlands, meanwhile, missed three of their spot-kicks with Justin Kluivert, Quinten Timber and Crysencio Summerville the unfortunate trio, as Morocco keeper Bono made himself a hero once again by saving the West Ham attacker's spot-kick.

Elsewhere, Brazil sealed a spot in the next round earlier on Monday after coming from behind and scoring a dramatic stoppage-time winner to beat Japan. Kaishu Sano had put the Samurai Blue in front on the half hour mark, but Brazil turned it around in the second half with Casemiro equalising before Arsenal's Gabriel Martinelli was the man of the moment, netting in the 95th minute to make it 2-1.

The knockout stage continues today as Norway take on the Ivory Coast, France face Sweden and Mexico face Ecuador at home.

Sports.title: Man Utd now have green light they need to secure £50million summer transfer
Sports.content:
Man Utd now have green light they need to secure £50million summer transfer

Manchester United could opt to step up their interest in a transfer target after a World Cup exit

View 2 Images Michael Carrick will hope to improve his Manchester United squad in the transfer window (Image: Marc Atkins, Getty Images)

Manchester United's pursuit of Crysencio Summerville has been handed a boost following the winger's World Cup heartbreak. The West Ham star squandered his spot-kick in the penalty shootout as the Netherlands crashed out to Morocco in the round of 32.

‌



The 24-year-old is among several Hammers players being linked with a summer exit after the club's relegation to the Championship. United are monitoring Summerville's situation.

‌



Much of the early summer transfer activity at Old Trafford has centred on strengthening their central midfield options. Michael Carrick's side moved swiftly to secure a deal for Brazilian midfielder Ederson and are keen to add further reinforcements in that area.

‌



However, the United boss will be eager to strengthen his squad across multiple positions as they gear up for their return to the Champions League. Summerville features on United's shortlist of left-wing targets.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

The forward's attention has been firmly fixed on the World Cup throughout the summer, having earned his place in Ronald Koeman's plans. Despite only making his international debut earlier this month, he featured in all four of the Netherlands' tournament outings, netting twice and contributing two assists.

‌



Man Utd ready to radically change summer transfer plan after Elliot Anderson race READ MORE :

Summerville's performances on the global stage have heightened the speculation around his future. United are reportedly facing competition from Paris Saint-Germain and numerous other clubs for his services.

West Ham have maintained they are under no pressure to sell their key assets, despite their relegation from the Premier League. The former Leeds United winger has three years remaining on his existing contract and is understood to be valued at £50million by the Hammers.

Summerville's agonising World Cup penalty miss could ultimately enable United to accelerate a potential deal. While some transfers have been completed during the tournament, the West Ham star can now concentrate entirely on his future, rather than chasing World Cup glory.

‌



View 2 Images Crysencio Summerville made an impact for the Netherlands at the World Cup (Image: ROBIN VAN LONKHUIJSEN / ANP (Photo by ANP via Getty Images)

The left-hand side of the pitch is an area of the team that Carrick may seek to strengthen in the transfer window. The manager utilised Patrick Dorgu in a more attacking position at the beginning of his tenure before Matheus Cunha claimed the role as his own. However, the Brazilian's adaptability also allows him to fulfil multiple positions in United's forward line.

The doubt surrounding Marcus Rashford's future could also influence any plans regarding Summerville. The England international excelled during his Barcelona loan stint and may yet rejoin the United squad after the Catalan side chose not to activate their purchase option.

‌



Should United choose to strengthen their wide options, the Netherlands' elimination opens the door for the club to accelerate their pursuit of Summerville. The Red Devils underlined the value they place on Premier League experience through last summer's signings of Bryan Mbeumo and Cunha.

Both players enjoyed impressive debut seasons at Old Trafford, and United will be hopeful that Summerville could follow suit. The Dutchman has already endured a whirlwind summer after making his mark at the World Cup, but with his tournament now over, United's bid to secure his signature could prove considerably more straightforward.

Sports.title: Man Utd ready to radically change summer transfer plan after Elliot Anderson race
Sports.content:
Man Utd ready to radically change summer transfer plan after Elliot Anderson race

Manchester United are set to change their recruitment approach this summer with Elliot Anderson's record move to Manchester City hiking prices across the market

Manchester United are ready to change tact with their summer recruitment given the hugely inflated prices for talent in England.

‌



The Red Devils are looking to ready their squad for a return to Champions League football and want to build on the momentum they built under Michael Carrick. They were among those keen on Elliot Anderson, who is now close to a £116million move to Manchester City.

‌



With a midfielder their priority they've also been eyeing up Mateus Fernandes, but have been left stunned by the £80m price tag that West Ham have slapped on him. Aston Villa value Morgan Rogers at £130m, albeit he is not necessarily a United target.

Adam Wharton is one man who has been linked with a move to Manchester but its understood that Crystal Palace see him as an £80m player.

Sports.title: Leandro Trossard delays transfer decision as Arsenal receive first verbal bid
Sports.content:
Leandro Trossard delays transfer decision as Arsenal receive first verbal bid

Arsenal forward Leandro Trossard could leave the club this summer after helping the Gunners win the Premier League title last season

View 2 Images Arsenal's Leandro Trossard is wanted by Besiktas

Leandro Trossard is set to assess his Arsenal future after the World Cup.

‌



The 31-year-old is about to enter the final year of his contract at the Emirates Stadium and his newly-rebranded agency FOKUS have been fielding calls over their client's availability.

‌



Besiktas have made Trossard, whom they attempted to sign last September, one of their top summer targets. Sources close to the Turkish club indicate they have already made a verbal offer for the winger worth up to €20million (£17.25m).

‌



Should the player indicate he is keen on the move, that is the kind of figure Arsenal would deem financially acceptable. For now, Trossard is firmly focused on Belgium's World Cup exploits as they gear up for their Round of 32 clash with Senegal in Seattle.

He would be keen to see out the final year of his contract at Arsenal but is thought to be realistic enough to know that a transfer could well be on the cards as the Gunners are looking to recruit a new left-winger - possibly two.

‌



At this stage of his career, he wants to play regularly and must also consider that his next big contract will be one of his last.

Saudi Pro League side Al-Diraiyah have also shown as interest in the Belgian, however, he may yet decide that he wants to remain inside Europe's top-five leagues.

A number of Italian clubs, including Roma, have made enquiries to sign Trossard in the past year, while Turkish giants Fenerbahce also previously tried to land the ex-Brighton attacker.

‌



Trossard was quizzed on his future several weeks ago ahead of Belgium's World Cup warm-up fixture against Tunisia.

View 2 Images Arsenal winger Leandro Trossard is currently at the World Cup with Belgium

He said: “At the moment I am still at Arsenal, so there is not much to say about that."

‌



The forward was then pushed on whether he could stay with the Premier League champions, to which he replied: “At the moment, yes. At the moment I am still at Arsenal and we will see what happens.”

Trossard mustered eight goals and 11 assists last season in all competitions and started the Champions League final defeat to Paris Saint-Germain in Budapest.

He has also been in fine form at the World Cup, scoring two goals and registering one assist for Belgium.

Article continues below

Last summer, he was handed a pay-rise to reflect his importance to Mikel Arteta's side but while changes were made to the terms of his contract, the length of his deal remained the same.

Sports.title: Ex England World Cup boss Sir Bobby Robson sent secret handwritten letter to village football club
Sports.content:
Ex England World Cup boss Sir Bobby Robson sent secret handwritten letter to village football club

EXCLUSIVE: Legendary England World cup boss Sir Bobby Robson penned a secret letter to a village football side when he was in charge of Barcelona in the 1990s

View 5 Images Sir Bobby Robson was England boss between 1982 and 1990 (Image: Mirrorpix)

An extraordinary poignant handwritten letter by former England World Cup manager Sir Bobby Robson has been found - 30 years after he posted it. Sir Bobby penned the note to a small Essex village club who were marking a 75th anniversary in 1996. He took time to write the letter even though he had just signed a contract to join Spanish giants Barcelona.

‌



He told Hatfield Heath FC: “The big guns need the little guns and you all do a remarkable job. I really admire your enthusiasm, dedication and devotion to the world game.” Hatfield Heath FC has kept the letter in their archives ever since. The club, which was formed in the 1890s, was celebrating its 75th anniversary of its affiliation to Essex FA. This is the first time the letter has ever been seen.

‌



Marcus Rashford could now STAY at Man Utd after showdown talks with club bosses READ MORE :

View 5 Images England World Cup legend Sir Bobby Robson with captain Bryan Robson (Image: Mirrorpix)

‌



Sir Bobby, who led England to the World Cup semi-final in 1990, wrote: “To Hatfield Heath Football Club You have probably heard I’m heading for BARCELONA FOOTBALL CLUB in my opinion the biggest Football Club in the world. “The stadium holds 120,000 people and it’s usually full!! There is not Barcelonas of this world unless there is hundreds of Hatfield Heath Football Clubs. Football has to start somewhere!

View 5 Images The poignant handwritten letter from Bobby Robson to Hatfield Heath FC

“It probably ends in Barcelona/Juventus/manchester-united-fc>Manchester United/AC Milan and Bayern Munich. But the Hatfield Heaths of this world provide the vase and the solid foundation upon which football and football players develop. “Believe it please! Good luck in all you do. The big guns need the little guns and you all do a remarkable job. I really admire your enthusiasm, dedication and devotion to the world game.” He signed off: “Congratulations on your 75th - you will make the ton easily.”

‌



Hatfield Heath’s secretary David Pyle said: “It was such a special letter to receive. A club member contacted several famous football people and Bobby was one of the few to respond. It really shows the class of the man.”

Sir Bobby died aged 76 in 2009. As well as taking charge of England he also managed Newcastle United, Ipswich Town and PSV Eindhoven. Respected author and historian Grant Bage, who spent six years researching a biography of Sir Alf Ramsey called ‘The Unseen Sir Alf’, said: “This is a really special letter. I’m an Ipswich Town fan and Bobby Robson is a hero of mine.

View 5 Images Hatfield Heath FC players and the 1946 Prisoner of War XI (Image: Ian Vogler / Daily Mirror)

‌



“The fact he took time to write a letter like this when he was leaving Porto to join Barcelona at such an important time in his career shows the measure of the man.

“Hatfield Heath FC are very fortunate to have such a lovely letter from a lovely man. Bobby was so popular wherever he managed - no more than his time in Ipswich where he lived.” Hatfield Heath has several claims to fame in football history.

View 5 Images World Cup rivals Geoff Hurst and Hans Tilkowski reunite to play a game of football with the original ball after it was tracked down by the Daily Mirror, at Hatfield Heath FC, Essex (Image: Mirrorpix)

Article continues below

On Boxing Day 1946 the club famously played against a Prisoner of War XI from a camp situated in the village. They lost 11-0 and marked the record defeat on its 75th anniversary in 2021. And in the same year Robson wrote this letter Geoff Hurst and West German goalkeeper Hans Tilkowski re-created the controversial 1966 goal on the club’s Calves Pasture pitch when the Mirror brought the 1966 ball back from Germany.

Sports.title: Barcelona's loss is Man Utd's gain as Spanish media send clear message to Michael Carrick
Sports.content:
Barcelona's loss is Man Utd's gain as Spanish media send clear message to Michael Carrick

Spanish media are struggling to fathom Barcelona's approach

View 3 Images Michael Carrick may end up working with Marcus Rashford after all (Image: Getty Images)

Spanish media outlets have questioned why Barcelona splashed out on Anthony Gordon rather than Marcus Rashford. Ahead of the World Cup, Gordon sealed a £69.3million switch from Newcastle to Barcelona, who turned down the opportunity to sign Rashford for less than half that figure, despite his impressive season on loan from Manchester United.

‌



Rashford could now be offered the opportunity to restart his Old Trafford career after his representatives held positive talks with the club. As for Gordon, while he charmed supporters and reporters by speaking to them in both Spanish and Catalan during his unveiling, his World Cup displays have led Spanish media to ask: Did they sign the right player?

‌



The 25-year-old was picked ahead of Rashford for the Group L opener against Croatia but was ineffective, while Rashford came off the bench to score the match-clinching fourth goal.

‌



Thomas Tuchel kept faith with Gordon for the bore-draw with Ghana but he again failed to make an impact before being dropped for the group finale against Panama, as Rashford was handed a starting berth. Having remained unused as a substitute, Gordon was unwilling to speak to the media following the match.

Get the latest World Cup news straight to your inbox by signing up to our Make Football Great Again newsletter now!

But he still attracted criticism from Spanish outlet ABC, which harshly noted that he "ran down the corridor of the mixed zone with the press faster than his attacks on the wing in this World Cup matches."

‌



Marcus Rashford could now STAY at Man Utd after showdown talks with club bosses READ MORE :

The same report suggested that Barca supporters would be "watching with concern what is happening on England's left wing during this World Cup."

It questioned why Rashford wasn't brought in instead. ABC pointed out Barca "paid a fortune" for Gordon, "despite the club's financial struggles."

View 3 Images Marcus Rashford's future is still up in the air (Image: Jean Catuffe, Getty Images)

‌



The article concluded by highlighting the "immense pressure" he faces owing to "the weight of his transfer fee, the challenge of joining a European giant, the scrutiny of the global stage and constant comparisons to the player who owns the opposite flank at Barca, Lamine Yamal.

"Being measured against one of the world's best is arguably unfair. Yet, it is to be expected when a club has just staked 80 million euros on you."

View 3 Images Barcelona media are concerned about Gordon's form (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Gordon also came in for criticism from Spanish media after earlier games. El Periodico branded him as "virtually invisible" in the Croatia game, while La Vanguardia described him as "subdued," although his defensive work did earn some praise.

It would be a surprise if Gordon was named in the starting XI against Congo, though Rashford, despite seeing plenty of the ball, failed to impress against Panama. Tuchel could alternatively turn to Eberechi Eze or Morgan Rogers on the left flank.

Sports.title: David Beckham’s wild reaction spotted in Wimbledon stands as BBC’s Andrew Castle proved wrong
Sports.content:
David Beckham’s wild reaction spotted in Wimbledon stands as BBC’s Andrew Castle proved wrong

The former England footballer was among the stars to attend the first day of Wimbledon on Centre Court, watching from the Royal Box

View 2 Images David Beckham was certainly enjoying himself at Wimbledon (Image: BBC)

David Beckham demonstrated to BBC viewers that even the prestigious Royal Box at Centre Court isn't above joining in with a Mexican wave.

‌



The former England captain was among a host of famous faces who turned out to watch the opening day of Wimbledon.

‌



He was on hand to witness Jannik Sinner defeat Miromir Kecmanovic in a gruelling five-set match. The world No. 1 and defending champion was pushed hard by the Serbian, who twice took the lead in sets.

‌



While the match itself provided plenty of drama, spectators at Centre Court sought other ways to entertain themselves during changeovers - with a classic Mexican wave proving a popular choice at the home of the All England Club.

As Sinner and Kecmanovic took their break between ends, BBC commentator Andrew Castle drew the viewers' attention to the ripple of excitement sweeping around the stands.

Novak Djokovic continues Wimbledon rampage with another pointed dig READ MORE :

Wimbledon commentator Andrew Castle's blunders as he steps down after 23 years READ MORE :

Castle said: “The wave sometimes dies around about the Royal Box, we can’t have that. Keep an eye on them," before saying, "Oh that's good" after watching Beckham join in.

‌



Beckham, seated alongside his mother, helped show that even the Royal Box occupants are happy to embrace a bit of light-hearted fun. And he wasn't the only well-known face to leap to their feet.

His son Romeo Beckham was also in attendance alongside girlfriend Kim Turnball. Beckham was seated next to the Duke of Kent, while television personality and baking legend Mary Berry was spotted nearby.

Notably, Beckham was also seated almost directly in front of opera star Katherine Jenkins, nine years after an email believed to be from the former England captain was leaked regarding Jenkins.

‌



View 2 Images David Beckham was not the only big name doing a Mexican Wave (Image: BBC)

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

An email to his advisor, which was leaked in 2017, said: "Katherine Jenkins OBE for what? Singing at the rugby and going to see the troops plus taking coke. F***ing joke."

Article continues below

Jenkins subsequently admitted she was offended by the email, telling The Sun in 2018: "I don't know why, again, that was aimed at me. I also don't feel the need to defend this, by the way. I know what I've done and when I got the OBE it was given to me for music and for charity."

Beckham finally received his knighthood in November last year, when King Charles bestowed the honour upon him for his services to sport and charity.

Sports.title: McLaren 'three months behind' rivals - Norris
Sports.content:
Lando Norris believes McLaren are "three months behind" in car development as they bid to get back to the front of Formula 1.

The reigning two-time constructors' champions already appear hard pressed to make it a hat-trick of consecutive crowns this year, given they trail leaders Mercedes - winners of seven of the season's first eight races - by 143 points.

Like all the leading teams, McLaren have regularly introduced update packages, of varying scale, to their car so far this season with two more revisions brought to the track at last weekend's Austrian Grand Prix - although the team did not use one of them, their version of Ferrari's 'Macarena' rotating rear wing.

But speaking on media day at the start of the Spielberg event, world champion Norris said overhauling their rivals was a longer process than the impact of single race upgrades.

"One good upgrade, no [is not enough]," said Norris, who is fifth in the Drivers' Championship standings.

"We need three, four, five, but it depends. Sometimes you take one little piece at a time, sometimes you try and make something so everything goes together because it's a new philosophy.

"We're like two, three months behind. That's not one upgrade; that's a lot of bits.

"I don't think we're going to be quickest anytime soon but hopefully over the next three, four, five months we can catch up and we can narrow the gap to be on pace with them."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the 2026 Austrian Grand Prix

McLaren proved their ability to make significant in-season ground during the last era of regulations and Norris added: "To catch up takes a huge effort from the team, which they're doing. Everyone is very excited and motivated because we know it's possible.

"We're like three months behind and that's a hard task to overcome but everyone in McLaren knows that we can achieve that and we're excited to try and do it."

'We want to be that team' - McLaren target Mercedes to emulate Verstappen title comeback

Norris and team-mate Oscar Piastri were dominating the championship this time last year but have just two podium finishes apiece to show for the first eight weekends of the sport's new rules era this year.

Piastri finished fourth with Norris seventh last Sunday in Austria, the former ending up 21 seconds behind George Russell's race-winning Mercedes.

Speaking on Sunday night, team boss Andrea Stella said it was clear they had to improve the car.

"We know from our side that we miss probably three, four tenths of a second [a lap], and we see this in qualifying, and we see this in the race," said McLaren's team principal.

"We tend to see pretty much the same pattern across different tracks. So it's a very consistent picture, and we know exactly what we have to do. We have to upgrade the MCL40."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Norris came face to face with his waxwork likeness at Madame Tussauds in London

F1's in-season car development race is proving especially critical this year, given teams are still able to find relatively big chunks of performance time in the early months of the new ruleset.

McLaren made a big jump when they introduced sizeable changes to their car at the start of May in Miami - which proved their best race weekend so far when Norris won the sprint and harried Kimi Antonelli for victory in the grand prix - with Red Bull the latest team to make big gains thanks to a sizeable upgrade of their own in Austria.

Given that trend, Stella says it is not guaranteed Mercedes will remain the fastest car all the way through this season.

So, taking inspiration from the way Red Bull caught up with McLaren themselves last year unexpectedly to take the battle for the Drivers' Championship to the wire, Stella hopes it is his Woking outfit who emerge as the chief chasers late into the campaign this time around.

"This is a battle of development for everyone," said Stella.

"Mercedes started with an advantage of a few tenths of a second but if they don't develop their car with another substantial upgrade, I wouldn't be surprised that in the second part of the season we see another team being the fastest car.

"We have seen in Austria already with Verstappen.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Craig Slater looks at the future of Max Verstappen at Red Bull as the British Grand Prix awaits!

"The important point will be how far ahead will Mercedes be towards the end of the season if there's another team catching up, will it still be early enough to actually catch up the points and for instance set a challenge like Verstappen set a challenge last year to us in the Drivers' Championship.

"Ultimately this is what drives our motivation we want to be that team and we want to be that driver that sets a challenge to Mercedes and to the Mercedes drivers in the championship.

"It's still a long way to go in the championship and the mission for McLaren is very clear - we want to be that team."

Sports.title: Brook: England Test captaincy would be 'great honour'
Sports.content:
Harry Brook has said it would be a "great honour" to take on the captaincy of the England Test side after Ben Stokes' abrupt retirement from international cricket.

Brook, England's Test vice-captain and white-ball skipper, was overlooked for the captaincy for the second Test against New Zealand at The Oval in the aftermath of the nightclub incident that saw Stokes stood down.

The England hierarchy turned to former Test captain Joe Root for that match, although Brook said that was "the right decision" at the time.

However, the 27-year-old Yorkshireman would now relish the opportunity to lead England across all formats if he is chosen to succeed Stokes as Test skipper.

"It would be a great honour to captain England at Test level. It's something I've always wanted to do," Brook said.

"The decision isn't up to me, but if it was offered to me I'd be happy to take it. I think it would be a tough job, but everything's tough in cricket. It's a hard sport.

Image: Brook was speaking to the media ahead of England's opening T20I against India on Wednesday, live on Sky Sports

"I've committed completely to England cricket. I've said I don't want to play any franchise cricket barring the Hundred. Whatever I do, on and off the field, is to try and perform as well as I possibly can for England. Hence the reason I don't play in the IPL and PSL and all the other franchise competitions."

Stokes has also identified Brook as his "natural successor".

"I like trying to be fearless and putting pressure back on the opposition," Brook said. "But the decision isn't up to me."

Brook insists he would be ready to unify the role of captain across all three formats were he to get the call and would enjoy working more closely with head coach Brendon McCullum, who oversees England's Test and white-ball teams.

Image: Brook is set to lead England in their white-ball series against England

"I love working with Baz, he's a great bloke and an unbelievable coach," Brook added.

"Some of the things he has taught me throughout my career, giving us the opportunity to go out there and play in the style he and Stokesy wanted us to play suited me to a tee to start with.

"It's been about evolving as a player, taking some of those learnings from the past and acting on them in games."

Stokes backs Brook for Test captaincy

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Stokes says he '100 per cent supports Brook' to take over as England captain and that it is a natural progression from vice-captain

Stokes has made it clear who he thinks should follow him as England Test captain.

"If I was asked who I think should do it, I would be throwing my 100 per cent support behind Harry Brook," Stokes said.

"There's absolutely no reason why Harry shouldn't be asked to do that. He's an incredible player, one of the more senior players in this group - we all know he's a phenomenally talented individual when it comes to his skill as a batter.

"If you lump a bit more responsibility on his shoulders with this team, we don't know if that's going to show any more improvement in the skills he's already got. Only time will tell.

"But you don't ask someone to be vice-captain if you don't think they've got the skills or the ability to captain the team when they need to."

Sports.title: What will happen to Usyk's heavyweight world titles?
Sports.content:
Oleksandr Usyk has dominated the heavyweight scene in recent years. He established himself as the pre-eminent boxer in the division with victories over Tyson Fury, Anthony Joshua and Daniel Dubois.

While he has never lost a professional fight, he has now chosen to vacate all his remaining world titles.

It marks a turning point for heavyweight boxing, with new faces and new names now vying to challenge for belts.

Sky Sports breaks down what will happen to the major championship belts...

WBC

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the explosive heavyweight clash between Agit Kabayel and Zhilei Zhang

The WBC has moved swiftly to anoint a new champion. Agit Kabayel, the German heavyweight, has been their Interim titlist since he knocked out Zhilei Zhang in February 2025. That made him the mandatory challenger for Usyk and he was due to box next for the full WBC championship.

With Usyk looking at other options and vacating the title, the WBC has elevated Kabayel and he is now their world heavyweight champion.

Kabayel has been cited as a potential fallback option for Tyson Fury if his fight with Anthony Joshua collapses. Fury is a former WBC world champion and is currently rated as the organisation's No 1 contender.

IBF

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Frank Sanchez found a massive right hand to demolish Richard Torrez Jr and put himself back in contention to face the best heavyweights in the world. Highlights courtesy of DAZN and Ring Magazine

The IBF has not yet ordered a fight for its heavyweight title. Frank Sanchez is its highest-ranked contender and the Cuban's team fully expect him to be able to fight for the vacant belt.

He would need an opponent, though. After Sanchez the next highest-rated heavyweights in the IBF's rankings are Moses Itauma and Filip Hrgovic. Itauma, still only 21 years old, is a hugely promising fighter, stepping up to world level to face Hrgovic on August 29. The winner of their fight could be positioned to fight Sanchez for that vacant belt.

WBA

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Murat Gassiev knocks out Kubrat Pulev with HUGE punch! Pulev vs Gassiev was the main event at IBA boxing at IBA Pro 13 in Dubai. Pictures courtesy of DAZN

The WBA already has a secondary or 'regular' world titlist at heavyweight in Murat Gassiev. Usyk was the 'super' champion, ie the full world champion and Gassiev will likely be elevated in the same way Kabayal was by the WBC.

"Oleksandr Usyk has said he will vacate his heavyweight titles, however, he must first submit his decision is writing to the WBA - only then will it be official. Once he does this, we fully expect Murat Gassiev to be elevated to super champion," Gassiev's promoter Al Siesta told Sky Sports.

"Then it is the goal of Murat to unify the division. However, first he faces a real test on July 11 against Tony Yoka in Moscow. We must not take victory for granted. God willing, Murat is successful - then we can move on and face the biggest names. Dubois, Itauma, Joshua, Fury. We are ready."

Who will take over?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Moses Itauma delivers 'beautiful' knockout to stop Jermaine Franklin in the fifth-round of their bout at Manchester's Co-op Live Arena. Pictures courtesy of X @DAZN

Last year Usyk vacated the WBO title. Daniel Dubois won that belt in his thrilling battle with Fabio Wardley. Dubois, a tremendous puncher, is expected to rematch Wardley later this year so wouldn't be able to feature in any unifications until 2027.

By then Itauma could have made his name as the coming superstar of the heavyweight division.

Former Olympian and professional heavyweight Delicious Orie told Sky Sports: "Kabayel is doing very well for himself at the moment, but if you're saying take over, I genuinely do think Moses is the man. It's not just the boxer that can be a world champion, I think it's the team.

"I know he's got a fantastic promoter, that's why I signed with that promoter. I think Frank Warren is a great matchmaker and I do think Moses will go all the way."

Sports.title: Cusack's Sheff Utd coach called her a 'psycho', inquest hears
Sports.content:
Sheffield United midfielder Maddy Cusack passed away on Wednesday September 20 2023; warning: contains content of a distressing nature. If you are affected by this story, please visit sky.com/viewersupport

Former Sheffield United midfielder Maddy Cusack's coach had called her a "psycho" and was playing mind games with her before her death, an inquest has heard.

Chesterfield Coroner's Court heard that Jonathan Morgan also made comments about Cusack's weight and relationship while he was the manager of United's women's team, which made her feel uncomfortable.

The 27-year-old was found unconscious by her father at their family home in Horsley, Derbyshire, on September 20 2023, and she died the same day.

Fellow professional Grace Riglar, who played for United at the same time as Cusack and was in a relationship with her, said the player was "anxious" about Morgan joining the club in February 2023 after her experience of working with him at Leicester years earlier.

She told the inquest on Tuesday: "I think it was stuff she told me about her previous experience prior to Jonathan coming to Sheffield.

"I think she said that they played a game against a team while Jonathan was the manager. She had done something on the pitch and Jonathan called her a psycho from the sideline.

"I don't think she let anyone know those types of comments affected her but they did and they made her uncomfortable."

She said Morgan joining United was a big cause of Cusack's stress, which coincided with her being unhappy there.

Riglar added that Cusack thought the coach made a "personal attack" on her by not putting her in the starting line-up for matches.

She told the court: "She was used to starting every game, she was an important member of the team. When Jonathan came, she was in and out from the starting team a bit.

"Her going from starting to being on the bench quite a lot, she saw that as a setback. That impacted her a lot.

"I just think she almost felt like it was a bit of a personal attack and that Jonathan was playing mind games with her by starting her one week and dropping her the next.

"She just felt those little things were intentional."

Riglar told the inquest that Morgan also made comments about Cusack's relationship with her.

When Morgan joined United, Riglar said, he told the players in the first meeting that if anyone was in a relationship within the team, they had to tell him.

Riglar said: "She found it uncomfortable when Jonathan would call me 'Mrs Cusack', especially in front of other players.

"We wanted to keep our relationship very professional. The football side and relationship side were very separate."

Riglar told the court that Morgan made a comment about Cusack's weight and she changed her eating and exercise habits, including by not eating carbohydrates, skipping breakfast and going for extra runs after training.

Riglar added: "She was one of the fittest players on the team anyway."

The footballer told the coroner that Cusack had become "paranoid" at the start of the new season.

She added: "She didn't really have anyone she could speak to without it getting back to Jonathan."

The inquest heard Cusack had a sick note from a doctor to have time off football and her marketing job at United.

She had also been prescribed anti-anxiety medication, the inquest has been told.

Cusack told her girlfriend before her death that she wanted to move to Dubai and be a flight attendant, and had been looking for a new job online.

Riglar told the coroner: "She didn't want to go back to playing football. I don't think she really knew how to get out of that situation."

The inquest continues.

Sports.title: Côte d’Ivoire v Norway: World Cup 2026 last 32 – live
Sports.content:

Glorious nicknames and the anthems are pretty good as well. Let’s belt them out, and we’ll be off in a few minutes. ♬ ♪ ♫ Proud Ivorians, the country calls us.

If we have brought back liberty peacefully,

It will be our duty to be an example

Of the hope promised to humanity ♬ ♪ ♫ ♬ ♪ ♫ Yes, we love this land as it rises,

Furrowed, weather-beaten over the water,

With its thousand homes,

Love it and think of our father and mother ♬ ♪ ♫ Share

Ivory Coast are a team who when I looked at squad before the tournament, I was surprised at the number of good players they have and they’ve done well so far beating Ecuador and almost holding Germany (although yesterday might be putting that result in perspective). Norway are favourites but I’ve got to think the resting of so many players against France and basically throwing that game has put them under enormous pressure today. Lose today and that decision will come under enormous scrutiny. I heard the great Phillipe Auclair on World Cup Daily mention a lot of Norwegian fans were not happy with that and something like that can puncture the feel-good mood around a team. Despite all that, I’m going for Norway to win 3-1 with Haaland getting at least two goals” – John “Will be an engaging match and both teams are quite physical and pressing in their game.
